answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a small refundable bond, returned only after random peer audits across several epochs verify its original work. One honest agent pays this cost once, but a farm with a thousand fakes must lock a thousand bonds and risks losing them all when audits catch copied answers. That turns each extra identity from a free bridge to rewards into a terrace of escalating losses, as visible as a signal fire on a knoll.
